case_title: Varinder Kumar v. State of Himachal Pradesh
statutory_provisions: NDPS Act s.20(ii)(c); Cr.P.C. s.100(4); NDPS Act s.50, s.52, s.57
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted on grounds of non-compliance with s.100(4) of Cr.P.C. and ss.50, 52 and 57 of the NDPS Act
high_court_outcome: Reversed acquittal and convicted under s.20(ii)(c) of the NDPS Act
offence_finally_established: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, s.20(ii)(c)
neutral_facts: The accused was apprehended with two gunny bags on his scooter containing varying quantities of 'charas'. The trial court acquitted the accused on the grounds of non-compliance with s.100(4) of Cr.P.C. and ss.50, 52, and 57 of the NDPS Act, citing that the seal prepared at the time of seizure was not produced in court. The high court reversed the acquittal, noting that the seals were marked as Exhibits PH and PK and that the recovery was from the gunny bags, not the person of the accused. The accused had a history of previous convictions, and the prosecution argued that the informant was also the investigating officer, which was a point of contention. The Supreme Court upheld the high court's decision, finding no violation of s.100(4) and that the law in Mohan Lal case should not be applied retroactively.
